method: Sample local bone rotations through glTF LINEAR quaternion interpolation at30/60Hz. Parent-coordinate angular velocity=log(q_next*q_current^-1)/dt, angular acceleration=finite difference of that vector. Moving samples require native ground speed>1.5m/s. Join windows are within one diagnostic sample of recorded neural segment start; other moving samples are within-segment.

proposal.method: Hemisphere-unwrapped quaternion component Gaussian smoothing with40ms sigma, then unit normalization; only named upper-body local rotation accessor values change. Not neural generation.

limits: Local rotation derivatives locate rapid changes; they do not prove their cause or establish perceptual quality.
Reference and robot differ in rig, degrees of freedom, running speed, style and clip duration. Scalar derivatives are descriptive rather than an equivalent quality benchmark.
Retargeted C08 includes a120Hz export bake; diagnostics cannot separate neural source, retargeting and interpolation effects without additional controlled runs.
Smoothing may erase purposeful arm action or alter hand placement; only a separate proposal artifact is created.
Center of mass requires mass distribution plus support geometry and dynamics; these joint-rotation diagnostics cannot certify crouch balance.
Raw G1 source, all published123takes and review storage are unchanged.

Quaternion LINEAR track interpolation creates knot-dependent derivative changes; acceleration percentiles depend on diagnostic sampling rate and original key spacing. These are discrete animation diagnostics, not physical joint accelerometer measurements.
recommended_controlled_followup: Generate one licensed human-locomotion target sequence using the bundled SOMA model and a matched G1 request; retarget both to the same avatar, hold sample rate, speed, source windows and cleanup constant, then compare arms and support/center-of-mass measures. Requires target representation conversion and new inference; not run by this diagnostic.
findings: Rapid local arm changes occur both inside generated segments and near neural joins. The measured upper-arm/forearm peaks are not confined to joins; this does not identify the source of the perceived jitter.
At60Hz during movement, upper-arm angular-acceleration p95 is about106rad/s2 and forearm119?129rad/s2. The optional40ms cleanup lowers these to42?55rad/s2, a numerical result requiring visual review.
The CC0 sprint has lower upper-arm but higher forearm acceleration percentiles under the same derivative calculation. It cannot be ranked as globally smoother from these scalars.
No crouch center-of-mass estimate or balance correction was made.
